title: Akka Tests Spec-Driven AI Delivery Across 65 Open Source Projects
gist: Akka tested a spec-driven AI workflow porting 65 open source projects, using 9.41B tokens in 99.3 hours with improvements in 57 of 65 ports. Sonnet was faster than Opus but used more tokens, higher effort did not help, and infrastructure/tooling ports degraded.

themes.theme: Scale and headline results of the Akka porting experiment

insights.claim: Akka ran a spec-driven AI porting workflow across 65 open source projects; the initial tranche took 99.3 hours and 9.41 billion tokens.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete cost/throughput benchmark for agentic code migration at scale.
insights.quote: The initial tranche took 99.3 hours and consumed 9.41 billion tokens

insights.claim: Akka reported a lines-of-code or performance improvement in 57 of 65 ports (about 88%), though this is self-reported by a vendor selling the tooling.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Strong headline but vendor-authored; treat success rate cautiously.
insights.quote: with Akka reporting a lines of code or performance improvement in 57 of the 65 ports

insights.claim: The methodology was staged: spec generation and up to 10% implementation across all 65 projects, then full implementation of 10 chosen for system characteristics and measurable results, which introduces selection bias into the headline numbers.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Full-implementation results come from a curated subset, not a random sample.
insights.quote: selected 10 for complete implementation based on system characteristics and measurable results

insights.claim: The delivery harness loops through discovery, specification, porting, benchmarking and improvement, with Claude plus Akka Specify handling implementation, testing and review.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows Claude embedded as the execution engine in a vendor's agentic migration pipeline.
insights.quote: The delivery harness cycled through discovery, specification, porting, benchmarking, and improvement.

insights.claim: Sonnet averaged 61 minutes per port versus 120 minutes for Opus, while Opus used about 40% fewer tokens, so the cheaper model was faster but token-hungrier.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Cost per port depends on token price times volume; model tier choice is non-trivial for migration workloads.
insights.quote: Sonnet averaged 61 minutes per port versus 120 minutes for Opus, while Opus used about 40% fewer tokens.

insights.claim: Higher effort settings raised token consumption without consistently improving efficiency, implying diminishing returns from maxing reasoning effort on spec-constrained tasks.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Budget controls on effort settings can cut AI coding spend with little quality loss.
insights.quote: Higher effort settings increased consumption without consistently improving efficiency.

insights.claim: A commenter argued the smaller model follows the spec while a larger model may improvise, matching what he saw in modernization work.
insights.speaker: Aaditya
insights.so_what: Suggests more capable models can be a liability when fidelity to a spec matters.
insights.quote: the small model follows the spec while a larger model may improvise

insights.claim: Open question: whether differences in porting efficiency stem from model capability, specification constraints, or both, since constraints could shape the result.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Confounded results mean the model-choice finding is not yet causal.
insights.quote: whether model capability, specification constraints, or both account for differences in porting efficiency

themes.theme: Specification structure as the quality lever

insights.claim: Structured specifications with claims, evidence and typed behavior improved first-pass implementations.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Spec quality, not just model quality, drives agent output; spec tooling becomes a product category.
insights.quote: structured specifications with claims, evidence, and typed behavior improved first-pass implementations

insights.claim: Remaining gaps were in context files around cross-component decisions; follow-up work covers interface enumeration, test ingestion, provenance tracking, differential testing and adversarial testing.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Cross-component architectural reasoning is where spec-driven agents still fail.
insights.quote: gaps in context files remained around cross-component decisions

insights.claim: GitHub Spec Kit similarly structures coding agent workflows around specification, planning, tasks, implementation and convergence, showing spec-driven development is converging as a pattern.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Multiple vendors converging on spec-first agent workflows.
insights.quote: GitHub Spec Kit similarly structures coding agent workflows around specification, planning, tasks, implementation, and convergence.

insights.claim: Validation combined original unit and integration tests with auditors for serialization, security, error handling, PII, idempotency and architectural boundaries.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Auditor agents on top of test suites is an emerging pattern for trusting AI-generated ports.
insights.quote: auditors checking serialization, security, error handling, PII, idempotency, and architectural boundaries

insights.claim: Akka added guardrails as failures exposed new issues, and each additional exit condition increased porting costs, a direct quality-versus-cost tradeoff.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Reliability of agent output is bought with tokens and time.
insights.quote: additional exit conditions increased porting costs

insights.claim: Applications, frameworks and libraries generally improved after porting, while infrastructure and tooling showed median degradation.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: AI porting looks safer for app-layer code than for systems-level code.
insights.quote: applications, frameworks, and libraries generally improved, while infrastructure and tooling showed median degradation

insights.claim: Akka reported a 143,333x improvement for Dify but conceded the compared workloads differed, making the figure not apples-to-apples.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Extreme outliers are likely artifacts; discount marketing-style multiples.
insights.quote: Akka reported a 143,333 times improvement for Dify, but noted that the compared workloads differed

insights.claim: Netflix Metaflow was approximately 100x slower after porting, a reminder of the downside tail.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Large regressions show unvalidated AI ports can be badly worse.
insights.quote: Netflix Metaflow was approximately 100 times slower

insights.claim: A commenter questioned whether lines-of-code reductions came mainly from dead code removal or from target-language differences, undermining LOC as a quality metric.
insights.speaker: Aaditya
insights.so_what: LOC reduction may not reflect real efficiency.
insights.quote: Whether reductions in lines of code resulted primarily from dead code removal or from differences in the target language.
